hook_patterns.name: Intrigue & Expose
hook_patterns.description: Calls out hidden truths or controversial claims about well-known entities right away to spark curiosity.
examples: Something is off about Susan Dell and I think we can all see why.
Here's what they're not telling you about Muse, Meta's new AI agent. I've been using it for a few

hook_patterns.name: Bold Personal Claim
hook_patterns.description: Presents a high-stakes personal or professional challenge in the first line to establish authority.
examples: Fashion trends move fast, but as a founder, I need to move even faster.
If you could please say 60 seconds, that would mean so much to me.

hook_patterns.name: Counter-Intuitive Observation
hook_patterns.description: Hooks viewers by stating an unusual or wide-reaching statistic that shifts perspective instantly.
examples: One in five people on Earth live in India, so when something works here, it can have ripple effects everywhere.
What year is it? 2026, 2019, 1448, Reh, we're 8 or 2686? 115, 115. Taiwan, North Korea, you both agree on the year.

hook_patterns.name: Direct Interview Question
hook_patterns.description: Jumps straight into an active conversation or on-the-street interview scenario without an intro.
examples: What course did you just graduate from? I studied computer science with AI.

on_screen_text_style: Short 2-4 word phrase highlights appearing bottom-to-center, bold sans-serif white text with black outline, synced phrase-by-phrase with spoken words to emphasize key nouns.
caption_formula: Short and punchy hook-driven caption under two lines, minimal emojis, 3-5 relevant lowercase niche hashtags.
takeaways: Lead with a high-stakes question or an expose hook within the first 3 seconds.
Maintain a fast speaking pace around 3.1 words per second with dead air trimmed aggressively.
Use bold, phrase-synced animated captions at the bottom center to hold attention.
Incorporate rapid b-roll or screen recording cutaways every few seconds to prevent drop-off.
